system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, the length per language in cell broadcast pages, encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

2 General description The CBS service is analogous to the Teletex service offered on television, in that like Teletex, it permits a number of unacknowledged general CBS messages to be broadcast to all receivers within a particular region. CBS messages are broadcast to defined geographical areas known as cell broadcast areas. These areas may comprise of one or more cells, or may comprise the entire PLMN or SNPN. Individual CBS messages will be assigned their own geographical coverage areas by mutual agreement between the information provider and the PLMN or SNPN operator. CBS messages may originate from a number of Cell Broadcast Entities (CBEs), which are connected to the Cell Broadcast Centre. CBS messages are then sent from the CBC to the cells, in accordance with the CBS's coverage requirements. A CBS page comprises of 82 octets, which, using the default character set, equates to 93 characters. Other Data Coding Schemes may also be used, as described in 3GPP TS 23.038 [3]. Up to 15 of these pages may be concatenated to form a CBS messagee. Each page of such CBS message will have the same message identifier (indicating the source of the message), and the same serial number. Using this information, the MS/UE is able to identify and ignore re-broadcasts of already received messages.

data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present, but neither version fits the UAE one-page limit: English is 3 GSM-7 pages and Arabic is 6 UCS-2 pages. The text also has no protective action, so the first page carries the hazard but not what people should do. The drafter can fix all of this by rewriting much shorter texts.

objections.issue: The English text runs to 3 cell broadcast pages, but the UAE handset requirement limits a message to 1 page. A GSM-7 page holds 93 characters, and the text has 221.
objections.fix: Cut the English to 93 GSM-7 characters or fewer, so it fits 1 page. Lead with the hazard and the action, for example: 'Dust/sand storm, visibility under 2km until 19:00. Stay indoors, drive with care. NCM'. Drop secondary detail such as wind direction.

evidence.quote: Message should be limited to 1 page maximum.
A CBS page comprises of 82 octets, which, using the default character set, equates to 93 characters.

objections.issue: The Arabic text is UCS-2 encoded, so each 82-octet page holds only about 41 characters. At 229 characters it takes 6 pages, far over the UAE one-page limit.
objections.fix: Rewrite the Arabic to about 41 UCS-2 characters or fewer, so it fits 1 page. Keep only the hazard, the action and the end time. Remove the source line and the geographic detail.

objections.issue: Neither language gives any protective action. The text describes only the hazard, its duration and the source, so the first page cannot carry an action.
objections.fix: Add a short protective action right after the hazard in both languages, at the start of the single page. Examples: stay indoors, avoid unnecessary travel, drive slowly with headlights on.

no_basis.concern: Even after shortening, it may not be possible to fit hazard, action and time into 41 Arabic UCS-2 characters. If not, an authority may need to grant an exception to the one-page rule.
